findings.title: Grav-ity of the situation: Unauthenticated Access to RCE in Grav CMS
findings.summary_md: The original researcher disclosure behind the flaw class used against Clop: Riyush Ghimire details CVE-2024-27921, a file upload path traversal reported to Grav maintainers on 13 January 2024 and fixed in Grav 1.7.45, chained with CVE-2024-34082 SSTI account takeover (fixed in 1.7.46) and Scheduler abuse for unauthenticated remote code execution. The post also documents Grav storing credentials and password reset tokens in flat YAML files under user/accounts and counts roughly 36,000 Grav admin login pages visible on ZoomEye. Date taken from the article's own '9 Oct 2024' byline.

findings.title: ShinyHunters hacks Clop leak site, threatens to extort ransomware gang
findings.summary_md: First news coverage of the breach: the attack began Friday night when ShinyHunters exploited what it claims is an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in Grav CMS to plant a text file on Clop's Tor leak site, then replaced the site with an Umbreon defacement. ShinyHunters claims full server access, theft of source code, Grav plugins, all files under /var/log, and the private keys of Clop's onion service, and demanded an eight-figure payment rising every 24 hours. Page shows 'September 19, 2026 09:48 AM' US Eastern; the site's RSS feed confirms the -0400 offset, giving 13:48 UTC.

findings.title: ShinyHunters Claim Hack of Rival Ransomware Gang Clop
findings.summary_md: Danny Palmer reports the incident came to light on the evening of 18 September and traces the feud to competing claims over the Oracle E-Business Suite zero-day CVE-2025-61882 exploited by Clop in 2025. It notes the stolen logs could reveal the IP addresses of people who connected to Clop's service, potentially unmasking gang members. Page is dated 21 September 2026.

findings.title: ShinyHunters hacks rival extortion gang and takes over its dark web site
findings.summary_md: Reproduces ShinyHunters' escalating 'Note to Cl0p' with updates dated 19, 20 and 21 September 2026, including the demand for Clop's earnings from the Oracle EBS campaign plus interest and a threat to disclose which companies paid Clop, how much, and to what Bitcoin address. It cites BleepingComputer's reporting that the initial access was an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in Grav CMS exploited Friday night. Article is dated September 21, 2026.

findings.title: When Criminals Hack Criminals: ShinyHunters' Breach of Clop and What It Reveals About the Ransomware Underground
findings.summary_md: Vendor analysis published 23 September 2026 that connects the incident to CVE-2024-27921, noting the specific CVE used against Clop has not been publicly confirmed, and recalls the TantoSec chain to CVE-2024-34082 for full unauthenticated RCE, with CVE-2024-27921 patched in Grav 1.7.45. It frames the second-order risk that organizations which previously paid Clop may face exposure of their negotiation records. Date taken from the page's 'Published on September 23, 2026' line.
